transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-15 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Samir Gupta (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Carlos Rivera, Dana Boyd, Ethan Park (Orison)

Summary: Quick sync to give Orison read access to Redwood's Trust Center, go over SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, explain RBAC/SSO options (SAML + SCIM), audit log retention, and KMS/HSM key custody model. Customer needs controls mapping and evidence examples for their internal audit team.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya: Hi Jordan, hi Priya, thanks. Maya here — security for Orison, and I brought Carlos and Dana. Ethan will chime in on legal later.
[00:22] Priya: Quick agenda: trust center access, what docs we can share (SOC2 Type II, ISO cert), how we map controls to Orison's matrix, RBAC / SSO options, and KMS key custody. Any additions?
[00:34] Carlos: Just want to make sure we understand data residency — which regions are in-scope for our workloads.
[00:45] Jordan: Totally, we'll cover that.

[02:10] Priya: Quick note on language — our Trust Center is tenant gated; we can create a read-only link for auditors or add individual accounts with SSO. The URL is usually like: https://trust.redwood.ai/ — we'll provide the specific tenant link.
[02:34] Maya: When you say "read-only link" is that temporary? Our compliance team prefers time-limited access and logging.
[02:47] Jordan: Yes, temporary links supported; we also add IP restrictions if you want. The link will have an access window and all activity is logged in our audit logs.

[05:08] Ethan (Legal): Sorry, quick legal q: Does the SOC 2 package include the SOC report and complementary user entity controls? And are there any redactions?
[05:20] Jordan: We provide the full SOC 2 Type II report for customers under NDA; some operational details are redacted (like internal IPs) but we provide the certification and testing period details. We'll attach the standard disclosure.
[05:37] Ethan: Ok, that helps. Also do you provide ISO 27001 certificate and the scope PDF?
[05:46] Priya: Yes, ISO cert is available in Trust Center — scope PDF included. For ISO we keep the scope file that lists services and endpoints in scope.

[08:02] Maya: For controls mapping, we need a matrix that maps our control IDs to Redwood controls and sample evidence artifacts (logs, screenshots, config exports). Can you show an example?
[08:18] Priya: Sure, I'll pull a sample. So, we usually map SOC2 CC controls and ISO clauses to Redwood control IDs. Example: CC6.2 — user access provisioning maps to Redwood-SEC-02 (RBAC + SSO). Evidence types: SCIM provisioning log export, SAML metadata, role snapshots.
[08:42] Carlos: SCIM provisioning logs — are those available as CSVs or API exports? We want to ingest them into our SIEM.
[08:52] Priya: We can export SCIM events and SSO events via API; we also ship a daily digest to the Trust Center. API has pagination and time filters, and a sample curl is in the docs (note: transcription sometimes says 'curl' like 'kerl'; but it's curl).

[11:05] Maya: Audit logs — retention and granularity? We need at least 12 months with immutable timestamps.
[11:14] Jordan: Default retention for admin-level audit logs is 13 months; we can extend to custom retention for enterprise contracts. Granularity is per-event with actor, timestamp, request ids, and before/after payloads for some event types.
[11:36] Maya: Is tamper evidence supported?
[11:40] Priya: Yes, logs are write-once within the retention window and we keep hash chains for tamper detection; we can provide a signed digest on request for specific time ranges.

[14:10] Carlos: On encryption, how do you handle keys? We have a heavy rule: keys must be under our custody (BYOK) and HSM-backed.
[14:22] Priya: We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS integration. You can bring keys into AWS KMS or GCP KMS and we use envelope encryption so raw keys never leave HSM. For particularly sensitive customers we offer an HSM-backed gateway for on-prem key custody.
[14:45] Carlos: Do you support rotation and key revocation workflows that produce audit evidence?
[14:50] Priya: Yes — key rotation events are logged, and revocation produces an evidence bundle with requestor, timestamp, and key fingerprint. Those bundles can be exported for audits.

[17:00] Dana: About RBAC: we need fine-grained roles to limit access to production model endpoints and to metric dashboards. How granular are your roles?
[17:10] Jordan: We provide built-in roles (admin, dev, auditor) and custom roles at the org and project level. For endpoints we have route-level permissions (invoke, manage, view logs). You can restrict token scopes to specific models or routes.
[17:34] Maya: Can we sync roles from our IdP?
[17:38] Priya: Yes — SAML + SCIM provisioning will sync groups and user attributes. We support group-to-role mapping so group membership controls RBAC.

[19:50] Carlos: One technical thing: we need to ensure our audit ingestion pipeline can get event IDs that correlate across requests end-to-end (client request id -> backend request id).
[20:02] Priya: We emit a request_id header and log it at each service hop; request_id is surfaced in the audit export. We'll include an example trace in the exported sample evidence.

[22:40] Maya: Data residency question: Are model artifacts and logs stored in the same region? We have EU-data residency constraints for PII-derived features.
[22:52] Jordan: We can pin data and logs to region X (for Orison it's europe-west1) for dedicated capacity. For hosted customers we have region controls and for dedicated/private deployments we can ensure complete in-region storage including backups. We'll map specifics in the controls matrix.

[25:30] Ethan: Regarding legal/contract controls: is there a standard DPA and can you support subprocessor lists?
[25:40] Jordan: Yes, DPA is in the Trust Center and the subprocessor list is exportable. We maintain an updated subprocessor registry with contract links and termination notice windows.

[28:10] Maya: A couple of practical items — our auditors sometimes want to run on-demand checks or ask for screenshots of config. Is interactive access allowed?
[28:22] Priya: We provide auditor roles with read-only admin views; if your auditor needs live session we can enable temporary elevated access with explicit approval flows and all sessions are recorded in the audit trail.

[30:50] Carlos: Do you have any controls that are currently out-of-scope for ISO? I recall a note about some operational controls that are not in scope for ISO 27001 but are covered by SOC.
[31:02] Priya: Yes, some host-level patching controls are handled by infra partners and are outside the ISO scope for the managed service; in that case we annotate the controls mapping to indicate "shared responsibility" and provide compensating evidence where possible.

[33:15] Maya: Can you show a sample of the SOC testing window dates? Auditors want exact test periods.
[33:26] Jordan: The Type II report covers Oct 1, 2023 to Sep 30, 2024 — we'll share the report with the test period boxed.

[35:55] Priya: One more KMS detail — for BYOK across clouds we support multiple key providers and a rotation orchestration that updates envelope keys without taking services offline; we record each rotation event.
[36:12] Carlos: If we revoke a key, do you have a plan/rollback?
[36:17] Priya: Revocation will stop new encryptions and we ensure rewraps for in-flight data where supported; we'll document the exact flows in the controls doc.

[38:40] Dana: About Trust Center access for multiple auditors — we have a leasing process where different auditors over time need access. Can we create timed auditor accounts rather than manage invites manually?
[38:52] Jordan: Yes, we can create time-limited auditor accounts and schedule expiration; we also support bulk invites via CSV or SCIM-provisioned groups for recurring auditors.

[41:00] Maya: A few possible objections from our internal reviewers: they will push on ensuring logs are immutable and on the ability to demonstrate BYOK without exposing keys. Any quick reassurances?
[41:14] Priya: For immutability we provide hash-chained logs and signed digests; for BYOK we never import plaintext keys — envelope keys are used and HSM proofs can be provided in the evidence bundle.

[44:20] Carlos: Competitor note — we've seen similar claims from BigCloudAI about in-region retention; curious how Redwood proves it.
[44:32] Jordan: We provide region attestations and the Trust Center includes deployment topology diagrams and exportable region manifest for your tenant. We'll include an example of a region manifest in the package.

[46:45] Maya: About evidence retrieval timing — how fast can Redwood respond to an auditor request for a given artifact?
[46:58] Priya: For most artifacts we can produce exports in under 48 hours, many are instantaneous via Trust Center. For deeper forensic artifacts it can take a few business days depending on scope. We'll queue urgent requests.

[49:10] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll (1) share Trust Center link & SOC/ISO artifacts (Jordan) by 8/18, (2) Priya to deliver controls mapping by 8/21, (3) customer to send final auditor list and region targets by 8/19, (4) schedule an evidence walkthrough the week of 8/25. Any objections?
[49:34] Maya: That works. A note: we'll need a short statement about retention for logs passed to our SIEM — whether hashes are preserved after export.
[49:46] Priya: Noted, we'll include retention + hash-preservation details in the controls doc.

[50:30] Ethan: One last legal ask — please include your DPA version and a note on subprocessor termination notice; we'll review.
[50:41] Jordan: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[50:50] Maya: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: transcription has occasional mislabels (Samir sometimes labeled Speaker 3) and a couple of acronyms are misrecognized (KMS changed to 'K M S' spoken), overall medium quality. Links referenced: Trust Center (link to be provided), sample controls matrix (will be attached).

End of transcript.
